I promised it a long time back, now it's time to deliver! The Squape Reloaded review:

THE LOOKS

First look at this thing is imposing. The box and presentation are imposing, and are exactly what a premium atomizer should come in. Sturdy box, tool, and disassembled tank are all in there, waiting for you!

The atomizer by default is tall, which is understandable given the spacious build deck and 5.2mL capacity. The pyrex tank is protected by the brushed steel housing which screws onto the base. It has some stylized engraving and triangular windows, but overall it's sharp and looks good with most mods.

The airflow control on the bottom is set up with a detented ring. The intake hole built into the base of the atomizer is partially covered by the various holes on the ring. Taking the ring off doesn't get you any extra airflow, so it looks like the 3.2mm hole is the same diameter as whatever next smallest part inside the tank is.

FEATURES

Besides the pyrex tank and airflow control, there are two big features that sets this apart from the rest of the bottom coil atomizers:

1) No rubber or rubber-based insulators on the build deck - all electrical isolation is done with anodized metal, so no matter how hot your build gets (hey, accidents happen!) or what juice you use, you don't have to worry about getting that rubbery taste that insulators can sometimes give off.

2) Changeable build decks - The anodized deck that comes with the Squape R (S-Deck) works with pretty much anything (cotton, silica, ekowool, and mesh). I use the C-Deck (Curved) because it gives a little bonus exposure to silica and ekowool, but still works great with everything else. The W-Deck (Wide) is designed for fat cotton builds, but I haven't played with that one yet. What's really great, though, is that these allow you to use whatever style you want regardless.

BUILDING ON IT

Building on it is pretty straightforward as it's a single coil: Your positive and negative captures are offset above a juice channel/airflow hole, and everything around is anodized, so you won't short out by touching the metal. For most builds, you'll want your coil to hang down from the leads, but with cotton, I let mine sit above. With Kanthal, the Squape R really rewards wide-diameter builds using cotton. Mine tend to overwick, and the extra cotton lets you have some retention. Vaperev have a great tutorial on a cotton build here.

Vapor production and flavor are excellent with a standard wide-diameter contact coil. For everyday carry, I really couldn't recommend anything else for performance. You can get Kayfun performance by tightening down the airflow, or a comfortable (but slightly restricted) lung hit with thick vapor and intense, warm flavor.

OVERALL

First and foremost, I would recommend this RTA in a heartbeat to anyone. Whatever you really want out of it, you can get it. You can make some decent clouds, or you can tone it down for a stealth vape. It's a simple single-coil build that you can pound out in a few minutes and be on your way. You can access the build at any time without dumping your juice, which on its own is an impeccable feature beyond Kayfuns and the like. Filling it is a little slow, since there isn't much clearance between the air chamber housing and the wlal of the tank, but that's entirely outweighed by the rest of the great features for a recommendation. Overall, 9.5/10.

Furthermore, the Squape Reloaded is a big step in the direction rebuildable tanks are going in. The market has largely settled on cotton as the preferred wicking material, but mesh, ekowool, and silica all have their merits as well. This is one of the rare tanks that allows you to use whatever you please (besides, I suppose, FC-2000 ceramic, but I haven't found that in over a year...), truly giving vapers another level of customization without a sacrifice in performance. My next tank review will be on another tank in this family that I just received this weekend: The Origen Genesis V2 by Norbert!
